biography.plain_text: Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani is Qatar’s Amir, head of state and commander-in-chief. Educated at Sherborne and Sandhurst, he served in the armed forces and held responsibility for education, health and national planning before succeeding his father. His public work has emphasised long-term development, international mediation and sport as an instrument of national engagement.

long_biography.plain_text:
Mediation has become one of Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani’s defining instruments as Amir of Qatar. As head of state and commander-in-chief, he represents the country abroad while directing national priorities at home. Qatar’s diplomatic role under his rule has centred on dialogue and negotiated settlement, alongside continued implementation of its long-term development programme.

Tamim was educated at Sherborne School and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst before joining Qatar’s armed forces. He became heir apparent in 2003, chaired bodies spanning education, health and national planning, and succeeded his father ten years later. Elected to the International Olympic Committee in 2002, he also oversaw the launch of National Sports Day, making sport a recurring fixture of public life in Qatar.
